title: Evidence Brokerage: Normalized Control Artifacts for Cross-Jurisdictional Audits
creator: Nora Patel
description: Create an ‘evidence brokerage’ capability that ingests heterogeneous telemetry and artifact sources (S3/GCS buckets, KMS audit logs, VPC flow logs, Console snapshots, Dedicated cluster metrics) and outputs normalized, auditor-ready control artifacts for SOC 2 and ISO 27001. The broker should: (1) map raw signals to canonical control assertions (e.g., logical access, key management, data residency), (2) attach provenance and retention metadata, (3) bundle artifacts per control and per jurisdiction with signed timewindows, and (4) provide exportable packages for external auditors and internal compliance teams. This ticket covers PM scope: control mapping schema, evidence bundle requirements, acceptance criteria, auditor export UX, and prioritization for initial regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). Engineering work (connectors, collectors, signed bundling) will be handled by ENG-48172 and sub-tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical control mapping schema (JSON Schema) is approved that maps raw signals to SOC 2/ISO control IDs and includes fields for jurisdiction, retention_policy_id, evidence_type, collector_id, and TTL
At least four evidence types defined and prioritized: configuration snapshot, access audit log, KMS key rotation proof, and storage residency snapshot
Collector contract documented: required fields, minimum retention metadata, and auth patterns for S3/GCS/KMS connectors
Evidence bundles can be generated via Console and include a human-readable manifest, machine-readable metadata, and a cryptographic signature/timestamp
Export flow in Redwood Console allows selecting region(s), control set (SOC 2 or ISO 27001), and time window and returns a single auditor-ready ZIP with checksums
End-to-end demo created for us-west-2 using synthetic data: bundle generated, verified signature, and upload to a secure reviewer bucket
Compliance team sign-off on schema and UX mockups and legal confirms export payload does not include PII by default
implementation_notes: Adopt minimal canonical schema to avoid long tail of custom fields; prefer extensible key-value pairs for vendor-specific annotations
Collectors should emit a small provenance header: collector_version, region, collection_window_start/end, source_uri
Retention metadata must tie to existing retention settings in Console (release: console-2025.04) so exports respect customer-configured policies
Use existing Signed Snapshot service (ENG-48172) for cryptographic timestamping rather than building a new signer
Provide an initial CLI tool (internal) for auditors to validate manifests and verify signatures
